title: Relative tensor and K-flatness under the internal-to-sectionwise module equivalence
statement:
Let $C$ be a site whose objects and morphisms lie in the coefficient universe. Assume abelian sheafification exists, its local equivalences are monoidal, and the category $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Ab})$ has the closed symmetric monoidal structure given by sheafified objectwise tensor over $\mathbf Z$ [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure, sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $R$ be a commutative ring object of $\mathcal A$, let $R_{\mathrm{sec}}$ be its reconstructed section-ring sheaf, and let
$$E_R:\operatorname{Mod}_R(\mathcal A)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_{\mathrm{sec}})$$
be the equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], which leaves underlying abelian sheaves and maps unchanged. Give the source the coequalizer relative tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] and the target the sheafification of sectionwise balanced tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $E_R$ is exact and has natural isomorphisms
$$E_R(M\otimes_RN)\cong E_R(M)\otimes_{R_{\mathrm{sec}}}E_R(N),\qquad E_R(R)\cong R_{\mathrm{sec}},$$
characterized on local pure tensors by $m\otimes n\mapsto m\otimes n$. These comparisons respect associators, unitors and symmetry. Applied termwise to cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $E_R$ identifies the direct-sum total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and preserves and reflects acyclicity, flat modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex]; in the internal category, flatness and K-flatness mean the same exact-tensor and acyclic-total-tensor tests.

proof.text: Naturality follows by checking pure tensors. The ambient relative tensor projection commutes with tensor maps and the sheaf-inclusion tensorator is natural. For triple tensors cancel the relative tensor projections and then the sheafification comparisons; tensor induction gives extensionality on triples. The relative associator and braiding formulas and the lax monoidal associativity and braiding identities of sheaf inclusion give the two corresponding coherence equations. The regular module has the original sectionwise action. The source unitors descend from the bimodule action maps, while the target unitors obey the lax monoidal unit laws. The adjunction triangle makes its unit comparison the identity on sections. Hence both unitor equations hold on pure tensors as well.

proof.text: Form the isomorphism of commuting tensor bicomplexes by the tensor comparisons in each bidegree; their naturality checks both differentials. Apply total.mapIso and compose with the inverse of the existing additive-functor mapTotalIso. Its coproduct-injection equation and the injection equation for total.map give exactly the displayed summand formula. No boundedness assumption is used.

proof.text: For each degree, use ShortComplex.exact_map_iff_of_faithful for the exact faithful equivalence. Acyclicity is exactness of these short complexes, so it is preserved and reflected. For flat modules use flat_iff_sectionModule from the existing flatness comparison; symmetry identifies exact right tensoring with the two-sided flatness condition.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, balanced-bilinear universal property; Tag 0GMW, lemma-sheafification-tensor. Internal-module comparison and passage to total complexes are the extracted agent argument.

proof.text: For a sectionwise acyclic test complex take its image under the termwise inverse equivalence. Acyclicity reflection makes this an internal acyclic test. Apply internal K-flatness, transport its total tensor by the constructed total-complex isomorphism, and use the counit isomorphism to identify the original sectionwise test. Conversely apply the sectionwise condition to the image of each internal acyclic test, then use the inverse total-complex isomorphism and reflect acyclicity. These are all the tests in IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients.
